events.title: The birth of St. Joan of Arc
events.shortBlurb: The Maid of Orléans, who would lift the siege of Orléans and see the king crowned before dying at the stake, was born at Domrémy…
body: By ancient tradition Joan of Arc was born on 6 January, the feast of the Epiphany, in 1412 at Domrémy, a village on the Meuse in Lorraine, the daughter of the peasant farmers Jacques d'Arc and Isabelle Romée. France then lay torn by the Hundred Years' War, and an English king claimed her crown.

From about the age of thirteen Joan heard voices she named as Michael the Archangel and Saints Catherine and Margaret, who charged her to raise the siege of Orléans and to lead the dauphin to his anointing. In 1429 she did both: Orléans was relieved on 8 May, and Charles VII was crowned at Reims on 17 July.

Captured at Compiègne in May 1430, she was tried by an ecclesiastical court at Rouen and burned there on 30 May 1431, aged about nineteen. A new trial ordered by Pope Callixtus III annulled the verdict in 1456; Benedict XV canonized her in 1920, and she is honored as a patroness of France.
